anomalies.obs: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the battery‑feed isolation diode U5 (SS2040FL) is drawn with its anode (pin 1, triangle base) tied to NET0020 = BAT+ (the node that also carries USB VBUS from J4.1, the barrel‑jack center from J7.1, and IC2 VIN), while its cathode (pin 2, bar side) is tied to the 18650 holder U9 positive terminal. The diode therefore points from BAT+ toward the cell.
anomalies.exp: The spec requires the opposite orientation: 'Battery (U7, 18650 holder) → pin 1 → Net-(U6-A) → U6 (SS2040FL) anode→cathode → BAT+' and 'netlist: anode on battery (via U7), cathode on BAT+'. The anode must sit on the battery side and the cathode on BAT+ so the cell can feed the rail while USB/adapter 5 V is blocked from back‑feeding into the cell.

evidence.quote: U6 (SS2040FL) anode→cathode → BAT+. ... netlist: anode on battery (via U7), cathode on BAT+
EthernetAndPower sheet: U5 SS2040FL pin1 (anode) wired to NET0020 (BAT+ node shared with J4 VBUS, J7.1, IC2 A2 VIN); pin2 (cathode) wired to U9 1043 '+' terminal

anomalies.impact: The 18650 cell is reverse‑biased and cannot power BAT+, so the board will not run from battery alone; conversely when USB or the DC barrel jack is present, 5 V forward‑biases the diode and dumps unregulated current straight into the raw Li‑ion cell (the exact back‑feed the diode was meant to prevent), a charging/thermal hazard.

parsed.summary: The battery‑feed isolation diode U5 is installed in reverse (anode on BAT+, cathode on the cell) relative to the spec's anode‑on‑battery / cathode‑on‑BAT+ requirement, which both blocks battery power and lets USB/adapter 5 V back‑feed into the 18650; other rail and switch connections (barrel‑jack battery‑disconnect, FAN53610 EN/MODE/FB, EPD charge‑pump values) match the specification.
